title: Mobility and Its Discontents
text:
Autonomous transport systems promise to reduce congestion, lower emissions and relieve the chronic shortage of drivers in many regions. Yet their deployment raises unsettled questions about liability when a machine, rather than a person, makes a fatal error. Insurers, manufacturers and lawmakers have yet to agree on who should bear that responsibility. In the meantime, cities are experimenting cautiously, often confining driverless vehicles to designated corridors.

Some ethicists argue that the more pressing concern is not safety but equity, since the cost of such services may favour affluent districts while leaving poorer neighbourhoods behind. Others contend that a reliable transport network could, paradoxically, expand opportunity by connecting isolated communities to jobs and education. The outcome will depend less on the technology itself than on the political choices made around it. What remains certain is that the decisions made today will shape mobility for generations.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what is the difficulty regarding liability?
options: It is unclear who is responsible when a machine causes a fatal error
Insurers refuse to cover any vehicle
Drivers are unwilling to share the roads

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do some ethicists consider the more pressing concern?
options: Equity in access to the service

questions.text: Why do cities confine driverless vehicles to designated corridors?
options: Because the technology is still being tested under controlled conditions
Because the vehicles are legally forbidden to exist
Because the corridors are the only roads available

questions.text: What does the author imply about the future of mobility?
options: Policy decisions will matter more than the technology itself
Technology alone will solve every social problem
Nothing decided today will have lasting effects

vocabulary.definition: legal responsibility for harm or damage
lasting for a long time or constantly present
fairness in the way things are shared or distributed
in a way that seems contradictory but may be true

paragraph_translations: Los sistemas de transporte autónomos prometen reducir la congestión, disminuir las emisiones y aliviar la escasez crónica de conductores en muchas regiones. Sin embargo, su implantación plantea preguntas sin resolver sobre la responsabilidad legal cuando es una máquina, y no una persona, la que comete un error fatal. Las aseguradoras, los fabricantes y los legisladores aún no se han puesto de acuerdo sobre quién debe asumir esa responsabilidad. Mientras tanto, las ciudades experimentan con cautela, a menudo limitando los vehículos sin conductor a corredores designados.

Algunos especialistas en ética sostienen que la preocupación más urgente no es la seguridad sino la equidad, ya que el costo de estos servicios podría favorecer a los distritos acomodados y dejar atrás a los barrios más pobres. Otros afirman que una red de transporte fiable podría, paradójicamente, ampliar las oportunidades al conectar a comunidades aisladas con el empleo y la educación. El resultado dependerá menos de la tecnología en sí que de las decisiones políticas que se tomen en torno a ella. Lo que sí es seguro es que las decisiones de hoy darán forma a la movilidad durante generaciones.
